evidence.note: After achieving parity (naive copy at 88.174 ms), the agent identifies the highest-payoff optimization first — prefix KV-cache for sampling, motivated by the JAX implementation caching the prefix rather than recomputing per Euler step. Distinct, hypothesis-driven, sequenced by expected payoff.

Experiment 1 (KV-cache) passes and improves 88.174→61.594 ms. Agent then proposes a genuinely different second experiment (torch.compile reduce-overhead) and first copies the passing checkpoint to /tmp before the risky attempt — deliberate protection of the current-best.

Experiment 2 (torch.compile) hangs during inductor compilation; agent aborts (C-c), reverts to the saved pre-compile checkpoint, and reruns to confirm the restored passing latency. Clean stop on a non-productive experiment rather than pressing on.

Stops after only 2 optimization experiments (far under the 8-cap), keeps the fastest passing implementation (cached-prefix, 62.311 ms), and records the trail to results.tsv/autoresearch_logs.md. No explicit '8-experiment' budget accounting is ever stated, and the final result remained slower than baseline (improvement_pct=-33.27) without exploring further despite abundant remaining budget.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it stays well within budget, runs two genuinely distinct hypothesis-driven experiments (algorithmic KV-cache, then torch.compile), sequences the higher-payoff idea first, protects the current-best with a backup, reverts cleanly when the second experiment stalls, and stops with the fastest passing implementation selected — matching much of the level-8 description of deliberate allocation and clean stopping at diminishing returns. It falls short of 8-10 because there is no explicit tracking of the ≤8 budget, only two experiments were spent, and it stopped with a still-slower-than-baseline result without leveraging its ample remaining budget to test further distinct ideas or justify the final trade-off. This places it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
